meta.title: PCB — Your Local AI Workspace
meta.desc: PCB is a local AI workspace for Windows: conversation, project analysis, task planning and file execution in one environment. Local, reviewable, recoverable. Open source, MIT.
lang.label: Language
hero.title: Where AI understands your project and work actually happens.
hero.lead: PCB is a local AI workspace for Windows. It brings intelligent conversation, project analysis, task planning and file execution into one working environment.
hero.lead2: From understanding a request and reading the existing project to planning the change, applying it and verifying the result, PCB puts AI inside your actual workflow.
hero.visual.caption: The PCB workspace: project context, conversation, plan and execution in one place
hero.alt: The PCB workspace: projects and conversation on the left, planning in the middle, files and execution results on the right
ws.title: One workspace, from idea to implementation
ws.lead: AI should not stop at a chat box. PCB connects AI to your local project, file system and tools, so a conversation can turn into finished work.
ws.chat.name: Chat
ws.chat.desc: Understand the request, weigh approaches, analyse a problem, explain code and errors. At this stage the AI only advises — it does not touch project files.
ws.plan.name: Plan
ws.plan.desc: The AI reads the current project, understands its structure and existing implementation, and produces a reviewable plan with steps. You inspect it, steer it, and decide whether it runs.
ws.build.name: Build
ws.build.desc: Once approved, the AI edits files, runs tasks and calls local tools, then reports what happened. Every change can be inspected, accepted or reverted on its own.
ws.note: From request to delivery, every step stays in your hands.
flow.title: Not another AI chat — a complete project workflow
flow.lead: PCB connects the AI, the project context and the local execution environment.
flow.context.title: Project context
flow.context.desc: Work against the real project: directories, files and the implementation already there.
flow.plan.title: Task planning
flow.plan.desc: Turn a natural-language request into concrete, executable steps.
flow.exec.title: Local execution
flow.exec.desc: Edit files, run tools and handle tasks on your own machine.
flow.review.title: Process review
flow.review.desc: Approve commands before they run, inspect changes after they land.
flow.revert.title: Change recovery
flow.revert.desc: Revert what you do not want, hunk by hunk.
flow.note: The AI understands, analyses and executes. You set the goal, make the decisions and give the final approval.
sec.title: Local first, with a clear boundary
sec.lead: PCB is designed so the user keeps control of the local working environment.
sec.local.title: Local service
sec.local.desc: The PCB service runs on this machine and serves the interface over a local address — no remote desktop, no cloud execution environment.
sec.keys.title: Key protection
sec.keys.desc: Model API keys stay on the machine. This website never collects or hosts them.
sec.auth.title: Execution authorisation
sec.auth.desc: Ordinary conversation never touches project files. Execution requires an approved plan, and running a command requires confirmation.
sec.trace.title: Traceable changes
sec.trace.desc: Every file change can be inspected, accepted or reverted hunk by hunk, which limits what automatic editing can cost you.
sec.tray.title: Runs on its own
sec.tray.desc: After the window closes, the background service can keep running to serve scheduled tasks.
packs.title: Two editions, one workspace
packs.lead: PCB ships as two Windows editions, matching two ways of working.
packs.desktop.name: PCB Desktop
packs.desktop.tag: For people who want AI to analyse projects, plan tasks and handle files directly.
packs.developer.name: PCB Developer
packs.developer.tag: For people who also read, write and adjust code. Everything in Desktop, plus:
packs.developer.p2: The current project opened as a workspace
packs.developer.p3: A dedicated editing and debugging environment
packs.developer.p5: The same core and project layout as Desktop
packs.note: Both editions share the same PCB core, the same AI runtime and the same project layout. Choosing one never changes how you work or requires migrating a project.
door.title: One entrance to your local AI work
door.lead: Analysing a project, rewriting a set of files or carrying out a complex development task — PCB gives all of it the same working environment.
door.line: One project, one workspace, one complete AI workflow.

faq.title: Questions
faq.lead: Seven answers about positioning, boundaries and cost.
faq.a1: PCB is a local AI workspace. It brings AI conversation, project analysis, task planning and local execution into one desktop environment.
faq.a2: omp is the AI runtime PCB uses: it connects to models and provides the AI capability. PCB owns the workspace, the task flow and local execution. The two work together.
faq.q3: Does PCB upload my project files?
faq.a3: File operations happen locally. Whether a model request includes project content depends on the task and how the model is called; choose a model according to its provider's data policy.
faq.q4: Will the AI change my files on its own?
faq.a4: Not through ordinary conversation. Changing a project requires an approved plan, and running a command requires a second confirmation.
faq.q5: What if a change goes wrong?
faq.a5: PCB can inspect, accept or revert per hunk. For important projects, keep using Git or another version control system alongside it.
faq.q6: Do tasks keep running after I close the window?
faq.a6: The local service can keep running in the system tray. Scheduled tasks belong to that background process, and a missed run is not caught up automatically.
faq.a7: PCB itself is MIT-licensed. Model usage costs depend on the provider you choose and its pricing.

about.title: About PCB
about.p1: PCB is an open-source project exploring how far local AI can go inside a personal working environment.
about.p2: We want AI to do more than answer questions: to understand a real project, make a reasonable plan, and finish real work under the user's control.
